OBJECTIVES:
By the end of this lecture students should be able to describe:


Sympathetic innervation of the thoracic viscera 

Parasympathetic innervation of the thoracic viscera 


@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Nervous System
The nervous system is divided 
into two main parts: 

the central nervous system
the brain 
spinal cord 

the peripheral nervous 
system
12 pairs of cranial nerves
31 pairs of spinal nerves 
and their associated 
ganglia
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Nervous System

The nervous system, together 
with the endocrine system, 
controls and integrates the 
activities of the different parts of 
the body.
Functionally, the nervous system can 
be further divided into:

the somatic nervous system, 
which controls voluntary activities

the autonomic nervous 
system, which controls 
involuntary activities
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Neuron

Neuron is the term given to the 
nerve cell and all its processes. 
The nerve cell has two types of 
processes, called dendrites and 
an axon. 

Dendrites are the short processes 
of the cell body; the axon is the 
longest process of the cell body.
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Spinal Nerve (Key to the diagram)
1. Lateral horn T1-L2 and IML (Intermediolateral nucleus) – location of 
preganglionic sympathetic neurons
2. Anterior (ventral) horn and LMN (Lower motor neuron nucleus) –
location of somatomotor neurons
3. Posterior horn - location of 2nd order sensory neurons
4. Posterior (dorsal or sensory) root
5. Dorsal root ganglion (DRG) – location of 1st order sensory neurons
6. Anterior (ventral or motor) root
7. Dura mater
8. Meningeal branch of SN (spinal nerve)
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Spinal Nerve (Key to the diagram)
9. Gray communicant ramus
10. White communicant ramus (T1-L2 SNs only)
11. Sympathetic ganglion and trunk
12. Splanchnic nerves
13. Viscera
14. Ventral (anterior) ramus of SN (spinal nerve)
15. Dorsal (posterior) ramus
16. Strip of skin innervated from one DRG (Dermatome)
17. Skeletal muscles
18. Blood vessels
19. Spinal nerve (SN)
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Autonomic Nervous 
System

The autonomic nervous 
system is the part of the 
nervous system concerned 
with the innervation of 
involuntary structures such 
as the heart, smooth 
muscle, and glands
throughout the body and is 
distributed throughout the 
central and peripheral 
nervous system. 

The autonomic system may 
be divided into two parts: the 
sympathetic and the 
parasympathetic. Both 
parts have afferent and 
efferent nerve fibers.
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Sympathetic Nervous 
System
The activities of the sympathetic part of the 
autonomic system prepare the body for 
an emergency ("fight or flight" 
response)

accelerates the heart rate

raises the blood pressure

redistribution of the blood: to the brain, 
heart, and skeletal muscle

inhibits peristalsis of the intestinal tract 
and closes the sphincters
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Sympathetic innervation 

Cell bodies of preganglionic
neurons located in lateral 
horn nucleus (IML) T1-T4
spinal cord segments

Preganglionic fibers synapse 
on ganglia of cervical and 
upper thoracic (T1-T4) g.g.
of the sympathetic trunk 
(postganglionic neurons)

Postganglionic fibers
terminate on the SA node, 
AV node, cardiac muscle 
fibers, and the coronary 
arteries

Activation results in 
increased heart rate, 
increased force of 
contraction, and dilatation of 
the coronary arteries
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Sympathetic innervation 
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Parasympathetic Nervous 
System
The activities of the 
parasympathetic part of the 
autonomic system aim at 
conserving and restoring 
energy:

slow the heart rate 

increase peristalsis of the 
intestine and glandular activity 

open the sphincters
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Parasympathetic innervation

Cell bodies of preganglionic
neurons located in the dorsal
motor nucleus of the vagus
nerve in the cerebral medulla.

Preganglionic fibers join the 
motor and sensory fibers of 
the vagus nerve and synapse 
on the terminal ganglia,
where cell bodies of 
postganglionic neurons are 
located.

Postganglionic fibers terminate 
on the SA node, AV node, 
and coronary arteries

Activation results in 
decreased heart rate, 
decreased force of 
contraction, and constriction 
of the coronary arteries
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Parasympathetic innervation
@ Dr. Olena, 2026

Supply of the thoracic viscera
THORAX
Artery: Internal thoracic & thoracic Aorta
Parasympathetic innervation: 
•Preganglionic: DMN of Vagus nerves, CNX
•Postganglionic: Terminal gg.
Sympathetic innervation:
•Preganglionic: IML (T1-T4), 
•Postganglionic: Sympathetic trunk T1-T4 ganglia, 
Thoracic splanchnic nn. 
Sensory Innervation: DRG T1-T4
Referred Pain: Left arm (MI)
